$comment: Product-intent confirmation record. Per the project brief, the INTENDED ASIN and the OBSERVED redirect target are stored in separate fields and are never merged. Blank means 'not confirmed from an official source', never 'assumed'.

retrieval.method: HTTPS GET of the submitted short link, following redirects; final URL and document <title> recorded verbatim
retrieval.tooling: Arena fetch_page (sandbox has no direct egress to amazon.com; resolution observed through the fetcher)
retrieval.note: Amazon listings render differently per session; a 'checkpoint/continue' interstitial was returned for one token on all three attempts.

asin_format_rule.statement: An Amazon ASIN is a 10-character alphanumeric identifier. Each of the five strings supplied in the brief is 9 characters, so none of them can be an ASIN.
asin_format_rule.evidence: All five submitted tokens measured 9 characters; every listing URL actually resolved by Amazon in this session carried a 10-character /dp/ identifier (B0CDY277D3, B09B7SB46R, B08DKYBTPH, B0DZFD6R9Z).

products.intended_asin_status: unknown - the brief supplies no product name and no ASIN; the token is not decodable to an ASIN by this project

aggregate_findings.note: Four of five tokens resolve, but none of the five strings supplied in the brief is an ASIN, and none of the observed final URLs carried a tracking tag. The set is a coherent kitchen cluster (3 air fryers across basket/dual-basket/oven-style, 1 probe thermometer, 1 unknown), which matches the brief's air-fryer editorial hypotheses - but that coherence is an observation, not confirmation of owner intent.
